sourceEvidence.label: SAPD Wiki local MCP certificate, TLS and settings evidence

assessment.summary: Keep the selected per-user App-managed CA, but centralize files, secrets, trust, Sidecar delivery and recovery under one transactional lifecycle owner.

nonNegotiables: Do not write LocalMachine or system-wide trust.
Do not place private keys, passphrases or shared CA material in packages or Git.
Require separate authorization before real CurrentUser trust or Codex configuration changes.
assumptions: No measured latency or memory budget was supplied.
The product does not resist an attacker who fully controls the same OS user session.
Web development validation precedes macOS and Windows packaging.

opportunities.title: Make the App the sole certificate and trust owner
opportunities.summary: Centralize identity generations, secret custody, restricted CurrentUser trust, Sidecar delivery and crash recovery behind one App controller.
opportunities.diagnosis: The current temporary TLS implementation and design contracts do not yet provide one durable owner for files, secrets, trust, active-generation selection and recovery.

evidence.claim: The selected design uses a per-user, per-install CA, CurrentUser trust and an encrypted leaf key.
The original C0 plan did not make secret transport and transaction recovery independent gates.
The current Web Dev identity is short-lived, stored in a temporary root and backed by an in-memory passphrase.
Encrypted PKCS#8 loading and unsafe secret-transport rejection exist, while production trust writes are fail-closed.
The AI integration page does not yet include certificate status, renewal or repair.
Without a sole transactional owner, concurrent operations and crashes can leave identity files, secrets and CurrentUser trust inconsistent.

desiredInvariants: Exactly one App controller can mutate one install/profile identity.
Every trusted or deleted certificate is bound to an ownership manifest, generation and complete SHA-256 fingerprint.
No passphrase crosses argv, environment variables, ordinary files, logs or unauthenticated IPC.
CurrentUser trust is explicit and constrained where the platform supports it.
Every operation phase can resume, roll back or fail closed without guessing the active identity.

options.title: App-owned identity with an ephemeral CA signing key
options.summary: Keep the selected CA model, delete the CA key after signing and add manifests, platform secret custody, restricted trust and a recovery journal.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It completes the selected lifecycle with explicit ownership and recovery.
It promotes secret delivery and recovery into independent gates.
It replaces temporary manual-use identity while retaining temporary CA tests.
It implements the platform mechanism behind existing unsafe-IPC checks.
It adds the missing user-visible certificate lifecycle.

tradeoffs.assessment: The CA signing key is deleted and trust mutations are centralized and fingerprint-bound, although CurrentUser Root still affects same-user processes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify CA-key deletion, restricted trust settings, exact-fingerprint cleanup and all unsafe secret-transport negatives.

tradeoffs.assessment: Generation and rotation occur off the query path; normal TLS startup adds only bounded manifest and trust checks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure certificate generation, Sidecar startup and first MCP connection against the current temporary identity.

tradeoffs.assessment: The manifest, journal and one inactive rollback generation are bounded.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare peak controller and Sidecar RSS during startup and rotation.

tradeoffs.assessment: A durable operation journal and one active-generation pointer make interruption recovery deterministic; full root rotation still requires user confirmation.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Kill the controller after every journal phase and verify resume, rollback and cleanup.

tradeoffs.assessment: Visible state, fingerprints and cleanup improve supportability, with added platform adapter and audit responsibilities.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run first-enable, repair, rotate, reset, uninstall and orphan-detection UAT on both platforms.

tradeoffs.assessment: The option extends the already approved design and can coexist with temporary automated-test identities.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Verify Web-first rollout, App upgrade preservation and downgrade fail-closed behavior.

residualRisks: CurrentUser Root remains broader than application-private pinning.
macOS direct App deletion can leave a public trust record.
Annual full identity rotation requires explicit user trust confirmation.

workPackages: Implement platform secret custody and one-shot Sidecar transport.
Implement transaction recovery, UI and lifecycle validation.
acceptanceCriteria: No real trust write occurs without separate authorization and exact snapshots.
Current Codex connects across restart and full identity rotation.
migrationNotes: Keep temporary CA identities for isolated automated tests only.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Restore the prior App implementation without deleting or regenerating a compatible durable identity.

options.title: Persistent encrypted CA signing key
options.summary: Retain the CA key under platform secret custody so leaf renewal does not replace the CurrentUser root.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It improves renewal reliability but changes the approved CA-key deletion invariant.
It still needs independent custody and recovery gates.
It provides durable identity but not the selected least-authority model.
It can use the same safe transport boundary.
It still requires the same certificate UI.

tradeoffs.assessment: A long-lived trusted signer increases the consequence of secret disclosure or signing-policy defects.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Threat-model CA-key extraction, signing API misuse, recovery and incident rotation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Leaf signing remains infrequent and outside the query path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure leaf renewal and Sidecar restart duration.

tradeoffs.assessment: One additional encrypted key and secret record are bounded.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare protected-state size and peak RSS during renewal.

tradeoffs.assessment: Leaf renewal preserves the trusted root and reduces user confirmation and reconnect churn.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Renew a leaf across App and Codex restarts without changing root fingerprint.

tradeoffs.assessment: The product permanently owns CA-key backup, corruption, recovery and incident-response responsibilities.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise CA-key loss, corruption and compromise rotation runbooks.

tradeoffs.assessment: It changes an approved invariant and creates a new high-value secret family.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review the threat model and obtain an explicit design decision before implementation.

residualRisks: CA-key compromise can mint additional same-user trusted certificates.
Name constraints may not be consistently enforced by every target validator.

workPackages: Add signer policy and compromise rotation.
acceptanceCriteria: Unattended leaf renewal is a confirmed product requirement.
Permanent signer custody passes security review.
migrationNotes: Requires explicit replacement of the selected CA-key deletion rule.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Before provisioning, discard the candidate; after provisioning, perform a visible full identity rotation.

options.title: Directly trusted self-signed leaf
options.summary: Remove the CA and install the self-signed loopback leaf as the platform trust anchor.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: It narrows signing authority but replaces the approved chain model.
It keeps the same lifecycle gates but changes platform trust adapters.
It provides durable identity without a CA.
It uses the same encrypted leaf key and secret transport.
It requires the same visible lifecycle UI.

tradeoffs.assessment: It removes CA signing authority, but trust-store semantics and scope differ by platform.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Validate exact leaf trust, EKU and hostname behavior in Codex, macOS and Windows.

tradeoffs.assessment: A one-certificate chain is not expected to affect the local query path materially.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare TLS handshake and Sidecar startup with Option 1.

tradeoffs.assessment: The design removes one public certificate and retains one bounded leaf key.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare identity storage size and peak RSS.

tradeoffs.assessment: Reliability depends on consistent non-CA trust-anchor behavior across target TLS stacks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run the complete Codex/macOS/Windows connection and rotation matrix.

tradeoffs.assessment: The chain is simpler, but platform-specific support and cleanup may be harder to explain.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype user trust, inspection and exact removal on both platforms.

tradeoffs.assessment: It replaces the approved chain model and requires new trust-store migration.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Keep the probe isolated until all compatibility evidence passes.

residualRisks: Codex or a platform TLS stack may reject or differently evaluate the self-signed leaf.
Store-specific leaf trust can diverge between macOS and Windows.

workPackages: Build an isolated leaf-trust compatibility probe.
Compare trust, hostname, renewal and cleanup behavior.
acceptanceCriteria: Every supported target client accepts the exact self-signed leaf design.
Platform cleanup remains exact and user-scoped.
migrationNotes: Do not write real trust until the compatibility probe passes.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Discard the isolated probe and retain Option 1.

opportunities.recommendation: Use the selected App-owned CA with an ephemeral signing key and add transactional lifecycle ownership; keep direct leaf trust only as a compatibility probe.

openQuestions: Do all target validators accept critical IP name constraints for 127.0.0.1/32?
Can a directly trusted self-signed leaf behave consistently across Codex, macOS and Windows?
Which macOS Keychain accessibility class matches the final background-runtime contract?
Is a maximum 24-hour inactive rollback window acceptable?
